english: Let $a$ be a real number and let $f:[-1,0)\cup(0,5]\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by
If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}f(x)$ exists, then the sum of the greatest value and the least value of $f$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$ एक वास्तविक संख्या है तथा $f:[-1,0)\cup(0,5]\to\mathbb{R}$ निम्न द्वारा परिभाषित है
यदि $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}f(x)$ का अस्तित्व है, तो $f$ के अधिकतम मान तथा न्यूनतम मान का योगफल ______ है।
solution: For $0<x\le5$: $\dfrac{\sqrt{x+4}-2}{x}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x+4}+2}$, so the right-hand limit at $0$ is $\dfrac14$
Left-hand limit $=a$; the limit exists $\Rightarrow a=\dfrac14$
solution_full: For $0<x\le5$, multiplying by the conjugate, $\dfrac{\sqrt{x+4}-2}{x}=\dfrac{(x+4)-4}{x\left(\sqrt{x+4}+2\right)}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x+4}+2}$. Hence $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0^+}f(x)=\dfrac{1}{2+2}=\dfrac14$.
The limit at $0$ exists only if the one-sided limits are equal, so $a=\dfrac14$.

On $[-1,0)$: $f(x)=\dfrac14+x^{2}$ is decreasing (as $x$ increases towards $0$, $x^{2}$ decreases), so it takes the values $\left(\dfrac14,\dfrac54\right]$, with greatest value $f(-1)=\dfrac54$; the value $\dfrac14$ is not attained because $x=0$ is excluded.

On $(0,5]$: $\sqrt{x+4}+2$ increases, so $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x+4}+2}$ decreases from values close to $\dfrac14$ down to $f(5)=\dfrac{1}{3+2}=\dfrac15$. It takes the values $\left[\dfrac15,\dfrac14\right)$.
So the range of $f$ is $\left[\dfrac15,\dfrac14\right)\cup\left(\dfrac14,\dfrac54\right]$. The greatest value is $\dfrac54$ (at $x=-1$) and the least value is $\dfrac15$ (at $x=5$).
originality_note: New: a two-piece function whose left piece contains an unknown fixed by existence of the limit at the junction, after which the range of the whole piecewise function (with the junction value omitted) is read off (way 5). Closest known: find a so that the limit of a piecewise function exists; the rationalisation limit (sqrt(x+4) - 2)/x. Different because: the parameter found from the limit determines the greatest value of the range, and both pieces contribute an extreme value.

concept_use.Piecewise-defined functions: domain and: Range of each piece: a + x^2 on [-1,0) gives (1/4, 5/4] and 1/(sqrt(x+4) + 2) on (0,5] gives [1/5, 1/4); greatest 5/4, least 1/5.
concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving non unifor: The function is defined by different formulas on the two sides of 0; equal one-sided limits (a and 1/4) give a = 1/4.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and the domain of every function introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with code by an independent route, unique and equal to the plan. Checked on a grid that the greatest value 1.25 and least value 0.2 are attained at x = -1 and x = 5. Changed: No change.
key_step: Using existence of the limit at the junction to fix a = 1/4, then combining the ranges of the two monotonic pieces.
justification: A limit of a non-uniformly defined function fixes the parameter, then the range of two pieces must be found with monotonicity; routine stages but no options, so 3 rather than 2. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q1 (L2) raised by the numerical format and the extra range stage.
